fields.description: The message this revision describes. Never changes once written - a revision that could be re-pointed at another message is not an audit trail.
fields.label: Message

fields.description: Denormalised from the message on purpose, for exactly the reason Chat Attachment.room is: the oversight read's membership filter must not have to join through Chat Message to find out which room a revision belongs to. Backfilled from the message in before_insert, so a caller cannot get the denormalisation wrong.
fields.label: Room

fields.description: 1 for the create row, then 2, 3, ... per subsequent change. Unique with message (created by patch, because Frappe's DocType JSON has no composite-index field), which is what makes 'two workers replayed the same edit' a failed insert instead of two audit rows claiming to be the same revision. Allocated by the writer inside the same transaction as the message update, never from MAX() outside one.
fields.label: Revision No

fields.description: What happened. Create is written once, at insert, so the trail is complete rather than starting at the first edit - reconstructing an original body from an edit's text_before works right up until the first edit that was itself lost.
fields.label: Change Type

fields.description: Which side made the change. Same three values and the same spelling as Chat Message.sync_origin, deliberately, so an operator reading both tables during an incident does not have to translate.
fields.label: Origin

fields.description: The originating side's own timestamp - Google's lastUpdateTime or deleteTime for an inbound change, converted from RFC-3339 UTC. Stored ALONGSIDE creation, never instead of it: creation is when we learned, this is when it happened, and the gap between them is the only evidence of a delayed redelivery. Ordering questions are answered by Chat Message.seq, never by either of these.
fields.label: Origin Timestamp

fields.description: Who made the change, when they map to an ERPNext User. Empty is legitimate and does not mean unknown - see Actor Email.
fields.label: Actor

fields.description: The Chat member's address when they map to no ERPNext User - an external participant, or a Workspace user with no account here. The same reasoning as Chat Message.sender_email: an edit or a delete we cannot attribute to a User must still be RECORDED, because the alternative is an audit trail with holes in exactly the rows somebody will one day need.
fields.label: Actor Email

fields.description: The body as it stood BEFORE this change. Empty on a Create row. THIS COLUMN IS WHY THIS TABLE IS MORE SENSITIVE THAN THE MESSAGE TABLE: superseded text exists nowhere else, because Chat Message.text holds only the current body and Google's tombstone is content-free.
fields.label: Text Before

fields.description: The body as it stands AFTER this change. Empty on a Delete row. Note that the delete itself is SOFT and Chat Message.text keeps the body (ADR §F.6.5) - this table records that the delete happened and who did it, it is not where the deleted body was moved to.
fields.label: Text After

fields.description: Free-text context from the writer - which reconciliation pass produced this row, which conflict rule fired, why an inbound edit was discarded. Never a message body and never a token.
fields.label: Note
